chunks: And he said: 'Everything which is measured by the sa' that reaches the awsaq, upon it is the zakat.' And he said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) made the sadaqa upon everything that the earth grows, except what is in the greens and the vegetables, and everything that spoils the same day.'

key_terms.أَوْسَاق: awsaq — plural of wasq, a unit of weight/volume; five awsaq constitute the nisab (minimum threshold) for agricultural zakat
key_terms.بُقُول: buqul — herbs and leafy vegetables; along with khudar, exempt from zakat due to perishability
key_terms.خُضَر: khudar — green leafy vegetables, perishable and excluded from agricultural zakat
key_terms.زَكَاة: zakat — obligatory alms-tax due on qualifying wealth and produce
key_terms.صَاع: sa' — a traditional volumetric measure used in early Islamic commerce, roughly equivalent to 2.75–3 liters
key_terms.صَدَقَة: sadaqa — charitable giving; here used synonymously with obligatory zakat on agricultural produce

ai.seo_question: What types of agricultural produce are subject to zakat in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: The Imam transmits two prophetic rulings on agricultural zakat: all produce measured in sa' that reaches the awsaq threshold (five wasqs, roughly 653 kg) is subject to zakat, while perishable goods such as greens and vegetables that spoil the same day are exempt.
